comment: Where the policy store is published. This file is CONFIGURATION, not generated state:
the base URL is carried in the packaged publication locator and served index, so relocating
the site is an edit here and a republish, never a code change. A GitHub project page is served under
its repository name, so the default already sits beneath one owned segment; publishing from
an organisation-site repository would remove that segment, which is what `pathPrefix` is for.
Nothing may be published at a root-level segment: a top-level /index/ or /policy/ would
collide with whatever the organisation site routes now or later. `layoutVersion` is in the
path so a v2 layout can be published alongside v1 during a migration.
The organisation serves a custom domain, so the canonical base is ts-defold.dev; the github.io host 301-redirects there and a redirect is not what an index should assert.
